verdict: Keurig Dr Pepper's sales leapt 71% to $7.34B after the JDE Peet's coffee acquisition closed in April — the legacy business grew a healthy 8.6% on its own — and net income was $952M.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +70.6% YoY, mostly the JDE Peet's acquisition

segments.name: U.S. Refreshment Beverages
segments.note: Dr Pepper, Canada Dry, Snapple, energy and waters — volume/mix +7.2% and pricing +3.7%.

segments.name: JDE Peet's
segments.note: The acquired global coffee business (Peet's, L'OR, Jacobs and more) — wholly incremental this year after the deal closed April 1, 2026.

segments.name: U.S. Coffee
segments.note: Keurig brewers and K-Cup pods — volume grew 6.9%, partly offset by 4.2% lower realized pricing; results also benefited from tariff refunds.

segments.name: KDP International
segments.note: Canada, Mexico and other markets outside the U.S.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Marketing, distribution and running the combined company — now including JDE Peet's global operations — plus $55M of other operating expense, mostly acquisition and integration items.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $474M (the debt taken on for the JDE Peet's deal), plus $47M of other expense, partly offset by a $400M one-time gain on selling an equity-method investment.

takeaways.title: A coffee giant is bolted on
takeaways.text: JDE Peet's contributed $2.65B of sales in the quarter and $289M of GAAP operating income ($480M adjusted, before ~$191M of deal and integration costs).

takeaways.title: A one-time gain flattered profit
takeaways.text: Selling an equity-method investment added a $400M gain below the operating line — a chunk of the quarter's $952M net income won't repeat.

takeaways.title: The interest bill jumped
takeaways.text: Net interest expense rose from $188M to $474M year over year — the cost of borrowing to buy JDE Peet's. Net income attributable to common shareholders was $810M after preferred allocations.

oneTimers: A $400M gain on the sale of an equity-method investment is included below operating income; JDE Peet's results also carry roughly $191M of acquisition and integration costs (its adjusted operating income was $480M versus $289M GAAP).
footerNote: Net income attributable to KDP was $882M (after $70M attributable to non-controlling interests); $810M was attributable to common shareholders after preferred allocations. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed.
